For tomorrow, define a narrow supported task, collect a small human-reviewed evaluation set, and ship a reversible baseline with abstention. Zero-shot prompting is fast for language tasks but needs evidence and output checks. Heuristics/weak supervision encode domain knowledge and are easy to inspect. Transfer learning reuses a pretrained representation with limited adaptation. [1](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/guides/rules-of-ml) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.10160)

Synthetic examples plus distillation can reduce serving cost later, but generated labels need independent verification and diversity; zero real labels means quality is not established. Compare correctness, coverage, latency, and cost on the same examples. Start with human review for uncertain cases and collect corrections for training. A launch deadline does not substitute for an evaluation baseline.
